messages:
liz: Quick help - PharmaCo wants a POC. They prefer PrivateLink but their infra team says they already route everything through a Transit Gateway. Asking for the cleanest path (PrivateLink vs peering) + a short onboarding checklist, and how we securely hand off an API key. POC deadline = 7 business days.

harry: TL;DR: PrivateLink preferred for cross-account + no route table changes, better DNS behavior. TGW complicates PrivateLink because endpoints live in the customer's VPC subnets; TGW can still reach ENIs but you must ensure TGW route propagation and attachments allow it. If they can't do PrivateLink, we fall back to peering or IP allowlist over NAT.

samira: Short presales checklist to give their infra (PrivateLink flow):
1) Customer creates Interface Endpoint(s) in at least 2 AZs in their VPC (for HA).
2) Use subnets that have capacity (/28 per AZ required).
3) Attach a security group to the endpoint that allows outbound to 443.
4) Share the endpoint IDs with us so we can accept (or set auto-accept).
5) Enable Private DNS if they want our public hostname to resolve to the endpoint inside their VPC.
6) Test reachability and cert name.

network-bot: PrivateLink gotchas: - If they route via TGW, ensure the TGW attachment supports interface endpoint ENI reachability (TGW route tables must include endpoint subnet CIDRs). - Endpoints consume IPs per AZ (/28). - NACLs must allow return traffic (1024-65535). - If they use strict egress rules, ensure the endpoint SG allows flow - PrivateLink is inbound to our service, but their services may still need egress for DNS/healthchecks.

harry: Minimal endpoint policy we recommend to restrict who can connect (replace with real vpce id):
```
{
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "vpce:Connect",
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": { "aws:SourceVpc": "vpc-abcdef12" }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
Note: Customers prefer aws:SourceVpce vs aws:SourceVpc depending on level of restriction.

samira: TF snippet (customer side) to create endpoint + SG (minimal):
```
resource "aws_security_group" "pc_vpce_sg" {
  name = "pharmaco-vpce-sg"
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  ingress { from_port = 443; to_port = 443; protocol = "tcp"; cidr_blocks = [var.restrict_cidr] }
  egress { from_port = 0; to_port = 0; protocol = "-1"; cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] }
}

resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_cp" {
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-REPLACE_WITH_SERVICE"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids = var.subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.pc_vpce_sg.id]
  private_dns_enabled = true
}
```
Replace service name and vars.

sec: Key exchange options (secure + auditable):
- Preferred: push scoped POC key into customer vault via short-lived, single-use presigned S3 upload or via their vault API (Hashi/1Password). We log the issuance with audit-id and attach to the ticket.
- Alternate: generate a key and mark TTL 24-48h, provide via CLI/secure share link. Avoid email.
- mTLS option: customer provides client cert to our SRE team; we can enable mTLS on the control plane for the POC (requires engineering lead/time).

harry: Testing & validation steps we hand to customer infra: 1) Create endpoints in 2 AZs and share endpoint IDs. 2) From a bastion in their VPC run: `curl -v https://control.redwood.local/health` (if private DNS) or `curl -v https://vpce-<id>.<region>.vpce.amazonaws.com/health` (endpoint DNS). Expect 200. 3) `openssl s_client -connect <endpoint-ip>:443 -servername control.redwood.local` -> check cert CN. 4) If 403 -> check endpoint policy, SG and that service side accepted the endpoint.

samira: If they insist on TGW + Centralized egress: ask them to ensure TGW route tables include the endpoint subnets and that IGW/NAT gateway placement allows DNS resolution of private hostnames. If their TGW blocks ENI reachability we can't accept traffic.

liz: What about auto-accept vs manual accept? Security wants audit trail, we prefer audit/logs.

network-bot: We can set the endpoint service to auto-accept for the customer's account only (in service settings), then CloudTrail still logs the CreateVpcEndpoint / AcceptVpcEndpointConnection events. If you want manual review, leave auto-accept off and one of us (samira or harry) should accept and annotate ticket.

sec: We'll tag the issued key with audit-id and push a CloudTrail link into the ticket. Also record the acceptance event id.

harry: If PrivateLink is impossible: fallback options - A) VPC peering (requires non-overlapping CIDRs, route table updates, no private DNS), B) IP allowlist via NAT egress (we supply egress IPs to allowlist), C) Dedicated/Private deployment (best for long-term, more setup).

liz: Great. Samira, can you turn this into a 1-pager for their infra and include the TF snippet + test commands + key delivery options? I'll attach to the SOW and ask for endpoint IDs or peering request id.

samira: On it. I'll also add a short section on TGW implications and ask them to confirm TGW route propagation covers endpoint subnets. ETA: later today. :+1:

liz: Thanks all. Will post updates once customer replies with their infra decision.
